name: Maple Tree
intro: A maple is a tree with pointed leaves. Its leaves turn bright colors in the fall.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A maple tree can be very big and tall.
Its leaves have pointed tips.
A sugar maple leaf has five main parts called lobes.
In fall, the leaves turn yellow, orange, or red.
Its seeds have flat wings, like little helicopters.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Maple trees grow in North America, Europe, and Asia.
Most kinds of maples come from Asia.
Sugar maples grow in the northern United States and Canada.
People plant maples in parks and yards for shade.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A maple tree needs deep soil that drains well.
It does not like very dry or very wet ground.
Young sugar maples can grow in shade.
Its seeds need a cold winter before they sprout.
Salt from roads can hurt sugar maples.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: Maple seeds spin down from the tree in the wind.
After a cold winter, a seed sprouts in spring.
The young tree grows a little taller each year.
A sugar maple makes its first seeds at about 30 years old.
Some sugar maples live for hundreds of years.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Maple syrup is made from the sap of sugar maples.
It takes about 40 buckets of sap to make 1 bucket of syrup.
A maple leaf is on the flag of Canada.
Maple wood is used to make baseball bats and bowling pins.
Bees visit maple flowers in early spring.

vocab.meaning: A watery juice inside a tree.
A thick, sweet liquid you can put on pancakes.
A rounded or pointed part of a leaf.
A small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
